title: Platform daily handoff — fractals sync (short notes)
body:
Context: quick 20m handoff to capture noisy state between shifts. Goal: surface anything that needs an immediate owner and avoid duplicate fixes. This is deliberately terse — use linked artifacts for deep context.

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Jin, Renee, Omar, + on-call SRE (Sam).

Topline metrics (last 24h):
- Avg control-plane p99 API latency: 78ms (baseline 65ms). Spike window 02:14-02:35 UTC correlates with quota recalculation job.
- Routing fallback rate: 2.1% (down from 3.4% yesterday after policy tweak).
- Auth token failures: 0.6% of requests (mostly transient 401s while KMS rotate was ongoing).
- Quota spillover events: 4 (customers hitting burst cap then routed to soft-fallback).

Control plane notes:
- Work in progress: allocator change merged to canary (PR: github.com/redwood/controlplane/pull/542). Canary showed 10% better KV cache hit but increased CPU soft faults on old kernels. Monitoring: watch kernel soft-faults and GC cycles. Marco to run kernel-symbol sampling and tag the canary hosts by 2027-02-12 EOD.
- Incident followup: quota recalculation job caused brief API tail — mitigation implemented (throttle recalcs, stagger cron). Still investigating why one shard took 4x longer. Linked: JIRA PLTFRM-1842.

Routing updates:
- Policy rollout: new cost-aware routing enabled for 30% traffic (alpha). Early signal: small latency improvement for short sequences but 0.5% increase in model-variant mismatches (customers saw slightly different outputs). Jin to check model-variant mapping tables and add a deterministic mapping for pinned customers by 2027-02-13.
- Observability gap: we lack per-customer routing trace IDs in the aggregator; Renee to prototype trace enrichment (sidecar) this sprint. Quick spike started today.

Auth & secrets:
- KMS rotation finished but some long-lived sessions hit auth errors. Root cause: session cache TTL not invalidated on rotate. Omar to add a TTL bump mechanism and run a targeted session refresh for affected customers by 2027-02-12.
- Temporary workaround: increased retries on auth client from 2->4 with exponential backoff; reduced visible 401 noise. Need postmortem for permanent fix.

Quotas & rate limiting:
- Burst algorithm tweak deployed: soft-cap now allows 10% extra bursts but requires backpressure signals earlier. Initial results: fewer hard-throttles but more soft-fallback routes; business okay with fallbacks for non-SLA customers.
- Action: create a short explainer for Solutions Eng on differences between soft-fallback and hard-throttle; Renee to draft and share in #se-onsite by 2027-02-14.

Blockers & risks:
- Kernel soft-faults on canary hosts could slow throughput if we expand canary. Priority: diagnose before wider rollout. (Owner: Marco)
- Deterministic routing gaps may cause pinned customers to land on incompatible variants. Impact: low volume but high trust. (Owner: Jin)
- Auth session refresh plan needs coordination with customer success for any forced re-auth flows. (Owner: Omar + CS)

Action items (owner — due):
- Marco: run kernel-symbol sampling, tag affected canary hosts, and report findings (2027-02-12).
- Jin: add deterministic pinned-customer mapping for cost-aware routing; verify no regressions (2027-02-13).
- Renee: prototype trace enrichment sidecar for routing traces; present spike notes (2027-02-15).
- Omar: implement TTL bump + targeted session refresh runbook; coordinate with CS (2027-02-12).
- Aisha: triage PLTFRM-1842 and schedule postmortem meeting; assign note-taker (2027-02-13).

Decisions made:
- Hold canary expansion until kernel soft-faults root cause is understood.
- Accept short-term increase in soft-fallback rate for customers without hard SLA while we tune quotas.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding an automated canary rollback trigger if kernel faults exceed threshold for >5 minutes.
- Could we do a targeted KMS rotate on a small customer subset to reproduce session TTL behavior?

Follow-ups for next handoff:
- Quick status on kernel sampling and any emergent mitigation.
- Demo of routing trace enrichment prototype if ready.
- Postmortem invite and pre-read link.

Meeting length: 22 minutes. Tone: pragmatic, focused on immediate ownership. If anything here needs escalation to platform leadership, flag in #pltfm-leads.

End of notes.
